official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 HRB application update
official_measurement_examples.fact: Building-control approval guidance for higher-risk buildings was updated 1 April 2026, including existing-building application requirements and remediation work categories.

official_measurement_examples.name: HRB threshold context
official_measurement_examples.fact: For the design and construction regime, guidance uses at least 7 storeys or at least 18 metres and specified building uses; scope must be checked against the applicable regime rather than height alone.

official_measurement_examples.name: Building control versus planning
official_measurement_examples.fact: BSR building-control approval checks building-regulations compliance and dutyholder arrangements; it is not planning permission or land-use allocation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Completion certificate gate
official_measurement_examples.fact: For higher-risk building work, completion-certificate approval follows completed-work assessment and inspection; prior building-control approval is not proof a completion certificate will be issued.

official_measurement_examples.name: Registration before occupation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A qualifying high-rise residential building must be registered before residents occupy it; construction completion and registration are separate steps.

official_measurement_examples.name: BAC trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: A principal accountable person applies for a building assessment certificate when BSR directs them to do so; registration alone is not a BAC.

official_measurement_examples.name: July 2026 BAC approach
official_measurement_examples.fact: On 9 July 2026 BSR announced a more proportionate and targeted building-assessment-certificate approach; this operational change does not remove statutory duties for occupied higher-risk buildings.

official_measurement_examples.name: Golden thread distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Key building information and golden-thread records support safety management and regulatory decisions; their presence does not establish title, planning capacity or permission to occupy where separate requirements remain.

core_rules: HRB scope must retain regime-specific building definition
BSR building-control approval is not planning permission
planning permission is not BSR building-control approval
building-control approval is not completion certificate
completion certificate is not high-rise residential registration
registration is not building assessment certificate
BAC application is not BAC approval
operational BAC reforms do not remove statutory duties
golden-thread information is not land ownership evidence
HRB status does not calculate parcel development capacity
historic BSR application status retains date and decision stage
remediation work can remain subject to HRB building-control requirements
occupation requirements are distinct from construction approval
absence from a public register is not automatic proof of non-HRB status
no Future Growth promotion while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official BSR, MHCLG, GOV.UK and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26. April and July 2026 HRB/BAC updates were preserved with planning, building-control, completion, registration and occupation-stage separation; no parcel promotion.
